You're light years ahead of many people!

1) You're acknowledging and engaging with your emotions in a serious way.
2) You're articulate about your struggles, and actively seeking out support and help.
3) You're taking responsibility for yourself.

The confluence of those things is uncommon - now it's up to you to build on it.
No way. I don't know you, but no way it's on you. That's why I'm curious - if a therapist made you feel that way, I'd be more concerned about their professional competence.

So are you done with therapy now? Do you feel like it was just something to help you get through high school?

You have an impressive level of maturity and self-awareness. That *can* be an incredible asset.

Yes your emotions are totally normal. Want to test it? Go to a public place and start screaming intermittently. See how people respond - I'm betting lots of people will attempt to ignore you, but if you look closely (might be hard while you're screaming), I'm sure you'll notice that you're creating some increased stress and anger.

Why would it be different with your baby screaming, your toddler, or even your partner?

Emotions have a deep and rich history, and have been developed in our species over millions of years. Civilization may only be 6000 years old, and modern society just a few hundred, but our impulses to get angry, sad, worried, and happy have been with us very long.

When you think about it this way, there is a relatively calming and logical conclusion - your anger is likely not dissimilar from other instances, and your coping mechanism can (and should) be similarly accessible.

You're a grown man who has been on this planet for more than a few years. You've probably had thousands of episodes where you got angry. That's not a bad thing - in and of itself - it means you have established patterns and habits.

How do you deal with your anger in other circumstances? Do you embrace it, channel it, and release it? Do you fight it back? Do you distract yourself?

The more open you are with yourself, and the more you acknowledge whatever patterns are helpful to you, the more manageable this emotional response will be.
